title: Cell Culture Practice (partial: the eight outlined lessons)
description: An eight-lesson partial package covering aseptic technique; media, supplements and reagent preparation; passaging; counting cells and viability; cryopreservation and thawing; contamination, mycoplasma and authentication; a bounded synthetic human pluripotent stem-cell maintenance loop; and records and traceability. All eight outlined lessons exist, but this is not a reviewed or measured cell-culture course: it remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only, has no project and establishes no competency, physical validation or institutional authorization.

prerequisites.statement: Laboratory Measurement and Solution Preparation, Laboratory Safety and Biosafety, and Foundations of Cell and Molecular Biology are recommended. This package establishes no university prerequisite equivalency.

outcomes.description: Estimate viable-cell concentration and viability from hemocytometer counts, accounting for sampling, dilution, chamber geometry and a consistent boundary rule.
Judge the reliability and meaning of a manual count: counting uncertainty, systematic preparation errors and the limits of dye-exclusion viability.
Perform an aseptic medium change in a Class II cabinet using pre-work checks, clean-to-dirty layout and sterile-to-sterile technique.
Interpret contamination evidence from visible appearance, sterility incubation, filtration and dedicated mycoplasma testing, and evaluate containment and antibiotic decisions.

Prepare a traceable supplemented-medium batch by calculating stock volumes, evaluating medium formulation, component suitability and QC evidence, and specifying filtration, filter-integrity checks, sterility incubation, dedicated mollicute testing, labelling, storage and release records.
Plan and document an adherent passage to a specified viable-cell target density, contrast it with suspension passaging by dilution, and interpret split ratios and population doubling level.
Plan and document a synthetic cell freeze–storage–thaw workflow, calculate medium, aliquot, DMSO and viable-recovery outcomes, and evaluate storage, quarantine and bank-tier traceability.
Diagnose synthetic contamination and identity scenarios by integrating visible clues, dedicated mycoplasma evidence, STR authentication, quarantine, disposition, source tracing and incident handoff.

Plan and document a synthetic feeder-free hPSC maintenance loop using morphology, feeding, density, clump-passaging, QC, consent and traceability evidence without implying physical-work authorization.
Reconstruct an auditable synthetic cell-bank, passage and lot-use history, then defend a bounded contamination lead and quality-system handoff from joined records.

lesson_objectives.description: Explain cabinet airflow, clean-to-dirty layout and the pre-work checks needed before an aseptic medium change.
Apply sterile-to-sterile manipulation rules: one cell line, fresh pipettes, closure handling, side approach, slow motion and glove sanitization.
Calculate and interpret a sterility-control incubation schedule within 20–35 °C, including the dual-temperature requirement.
Distinguish visible turbidity, standard sterility incubation, 0.22 µm filtration and dedicated mycoplasma testing.
Evaluate contamination responses, including containment, waste decontamination and the limits of antibiotics.
Prepare a representative counting sample and calculate the overall dilution factor, including non-twofold and two-step dilutions.
Relate Improved-Neubauer geometry to the volume counted, and apply a consistent boundary rule that is kept separate from the stain decision.
Calculate viable-cell concentration and percent viability from two-chamber tallies.
Estimate Poisson counting uncertainty from the number of cells counted, state its assumptions, and plan how many squares to count for a target precision.
Interpret chamber disagreement, sparse or crowded fields and trypan-blue results, distinguishing counting error from systematic error and membrane integrity from overall cell health.
Explain the roles of basal-medium nutrients, osmolality, pH, bicarbonate/CO₂ buffering and phenol red, and distinguish serum-containing, serum-free and chemically defined systems.
Calculate supplement-stock and basal-medium volumes from stock and target concentrations using the finished batch volume.
Evaluate supplement handling, including L-glutamine instability, frozen single-use aliquots, serum heat-inactivation and media dedicated to one cell line.
Plan a 0.22 µm filter-sterilization and integrity-check workflow and distinguish filtration, visible clarity and dedicated mollicute evidence.
Specify QC, sterility-control incubation, traceable labels, aliquot accounting, expiry, light-protected 2–8 °C storage and quarantine for a supplemented-medium batch.
Evaluate confluence or suspension density, morphology and viability evidence to decide whether a synthetic culture should be passaged, held for investigation or discarded under the scenario's rule.
Explain adherent detachment, washing, dissociation-reagent neutralization and resuspension, and contrast them with suspension passaging by direct dilution or transfer of a culture portion.
Calculate viable-cell concentration, required cell-suspension volume and fresh-medium volume for a specified viable-cell target and final culture volume.
Distinguish split ratio from target-density seeding, and calculate population doubling level and cumulative population doubling level from starting and harvested cell numbers.
Evaluate passage records and the risks of repeated subculture, including the need for later authentication and the limits of numerical or simulated evidence.
Distinguish permeating from non-permeating cryoprotectants, and relate DMSO concentration, cold dropwise handling and removal to freezing protection, osmotic stress and toxicity.
Explain the two-factor account of freezing injury and use it to justify controlled cooling, an appropriate passive container or controlled-rate device, and rapid thawing.
Calculate freeze-medium component volumes, vial counts and concentrations, post-thaw dilution and residual DMSO fractions, and viable-cell recovery.
Evaluate vapour- versus liquid-phase nitrogen storage, fast-thaw and recount decisions, including the safety rationale and limits of dye-exclusion viability.
Evaluate quarantine, quality-control status, storage-location records and bank-tier links without treating a simulation result as a release decision.
Recognise visible bacterial and fungal clue patterns and connect contamination response to plausible routes without claiming species identification from appearance.
Explain why mycoplasma can remain invisible and compare culture, nucleic-acid amplification and DNA-stain evidence, including method-specific limits and controls.
Apply quarantine before identification, choose discard versus bounded rescue referral, reject antibiotic masking and prepare an incident handoff.
Explain HeLa-era cross-contamination context and interpret synthetic STR loci and allele calls, distinguishing match evidence from mismatch and from proof of purity or phenotype.
Plan incoming-line quarantine, contamination and identity testing, and trace shared medium, equipment, handling and receipt records as alternative source hypotheses.
Explain defined-matrix feeder-free hPSC maintenance and evaluate coating, handling, drying and lot traceability.
Interpret synthetic colony morphology and density, selectively remove differentiated areas, and use observation, feeding and density evidence for passage decisions.
Justify gentle small-clump rather than default single-cell passaging and calculate clump allocations across destination wells.
Distinguish intake and periodic mycoplasma, STR-identity, karyotype and undifferentiated-marker QC, including quarantine clearance and assay limits.
Evaluate consent/transfer restrictions, permissible-use boundaries, privacy and records connecting materials, maintenance actions, deviations and QC.
Distinguish master and working cell-bank tiers and preserve parent–child provenance for bank, vial, passage, relocation and derivative records.
Reconcile passage and population-doubling-level ledgers from raw viable-cell numbers, preserving interval calculations, cumulative values and transparent corrections.
Join vessel, preparation and lot records across media, reagents and matrices to enumerate shared exposures and evaluate a contamination lead without claiming causation.
Evaluate label-to-ledger identifiers and corrections using attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original and accurate (ALCOA) record principles.
Construct an outline-only contamination incident/deviation handoff with reproducible scope and evidence, handing deeper quality-system, GLP and CLIA instruction to planned layer 4.

duration.equivalent_structure: A proposed, unmeasured eight-week partial block with one outlined lesson per week in the established minimal-churn order; not a reviewed workload or a complete course.

weeks.title: Aseptic technique (outline lesson 1); bench practice: aseptic medium change with hidden contamination
Counting cells and viability (outline lesson 4); bench practice: hemocytometer count with trypan blue
Media, supplements and reagent preparation (outline lesson 2); bench practice: filter-sterilize and QC a supplemented medium
Passaging adherent and suspension cells (outline lesson 3); bench practice: passage an adherent line to a target density
Cryopreservation and thawing (outline lesson 5); bench practice: freeze and thaw with viability outcomes

lessons.title: Aseptic technique and a medium change with hidden contamination
lessons.worked_example: For one T-75 change, inspect the supplies, reject the expired lot, wipe the empty cabinet with sterile 70% alcohol, arrange clean supplies, target flask and dirty items from clean to dirty, remove spent medium with a fresh pipette, decontaminate and remove the waste, add 12 mL from the in-date lot, draw sterility controls, incubate 7 days at 22 °C then 7 days at 32 °C, submit a dedicated mycoplasma assay, dispose of the turbid flask sealed and decontaminated, and finish with a sterile wipe. If the fresh-medium control becomes turbid or the mycoplasma assay is positive, a clear culture appearance is not proof of sterility.

lessons.title: Counting cells and viability with a hemocytometer
lessons.worked_example: Twenty microlitres of suspension plus 30 µL of trypan blue give a dilution factor of 50/20 = 2.5. Eight large squares hold 245 unstained and 36 stained included cells, so viable cells/mL = 245/8 × 10,000 × 2.5 = 7.66 × 10⁵, viability = 245/281 = 87.2%, and the Poisson uncertainty of the total count is 100/√281 = 5.97%.

lessons.title: Media, supplements and reagent preparation with filtration and QC
lessons.worked_example: For the synthetic 500 mL final batch, serum = 0.10 × 500 = 50 mL, 100× glutamine stock = 500/100 = 5 mL (equivalently 2 × 500/200), and basal medium = 500 − 50 − 5 = 445 mL; the explicitly approximate osmolality estimate is (445 × 290 + 50 × 300 + 5 × 400)/500 = 292.1 mOsm/kg, reported to three significant figures as 292 mOsm/kg.

lessons.title: Passaging adherent and suspension cells
lessons.worked_example: A 10 µL + 10 µL count gives 58 + 63 = 121 unstained and 5 + 4 = 9 stained cells across two 10⁻⁴ mL squares: viable concentration = (121/2) × 10,000 × 2 = 1.21 × 10⁶ cells/mL and viability = 121/130 × 100 = 93.1%. Each of two T-75 flasks targeting 5.00 × 10⁵ viable cells in 12.0 mL needs 0.413223 mL suspension plus 11.586777 mL fresh medium. The 7.26 × 10⁶ viable harvest from N0 = 1.815 × 10⁶ adds log₂4 = 2 PDL, taking cumulative PDL 18 to 20.

lessons.title: Cryopreservation and thawing
lessons.worked_example: A 5.00 mL harvest at 2.00 × 10⁶ viable cells/mL and 95.0% viability supplies 1.00 × 10⁷ viable cells for four 1.00 mL vials, each containing 2.50 × 10⁶ viable cells per vial; the separate batch concentration is 2.50 × 10⁶ cells/mL. A 4.00 mL final batch at 10.0% DMSO needs 0.400 mL DMSO + 3.60 mL base. One vial diluted into 9.00 mL medium reaches 1.00% DMSO; 95.0% solute removal and resuspension in 2.00 mL leaves 0.250%. At 92.0% post-thaw viability with total cells conserved, recovery = 2.50 × 10⁶ × 92.0/95.0 = 2.421053 × 10⁶ viable cells and 1.210526 × 10⁶ cells/mL.

lessons.title: Contamination, mycoplasma and cell-line authentication
lessons.worked_example: At four synthetic STR loci, sample [8,8], [10,11], [12,14], [7,9] and reference [8,9], [10,11], [12,12], [7,9] share 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 6 allele-call observations. The lesson-defined classroom shared-call percentage is 100 × 6/8 = 75.0%, an arithmetic exercise rather than the Tanabe or Masters algorithm or an authentication threshold. Clear flasks still require dedicated mycoplasma and STR evidence before disposition.

lessons.title: Human pluripotent stem cells: maintenance, morphology and quality control
lessons.worked_example: For a 240 mm² panel with 18 mm² differentiated area and 15 mm² removed, residual differentiated area = (18−15)/240 × 100 = 1.25%. A 156-clump harvest allocated to six wells gives 156/6 = 26 clumps per well. A synthetic five-passage periodic-QC interval after passage 8 places the next bundle at passage 8+5 = 13. All values are simulation choices.

lessons.title: Records and traceability
lessons.worked_example: Joining four positive vessels through preparations P-401/P-402/P-405 and medium batches F-31/F-32 resolves every positive to basal-medium lot BM-24-118, while negative V-104 shares that exposure and therefore prevents a causal overclaim; the linked passage ledger adds log₂(2.50/1.25) = 1 and log₂(3.00/0.75) = 2 to PDL 8.0, yielding 11.0.

grading_policy.attempt_policy: Unlimited formative retries; no summative grade is awarded.
grading_policy.solution_release: Public practice solutions may be shown after an attempt. They are not production exam keys.
grading_policy.late_policy: No deadlines or late penalties exist in this partial package.
grading_policy.appeals: No instructor review workflow is implemented; report ambiguous practice items as content issues.

accessibility.diagram_policy: The package contains no diagrams; aseptic layout, medium preparation, passaging and counting rules are given in text and tables. All seven bench simulations use text panels and event logs; the hemocytometer simulation additionally provides a text list of every synthetic cell alongside its drawn field.
known_issues: Unicode equations require structured mathematical alternatives and assistive-technology review.
The bench simulations' panels, fields and text alternatives have not been reviewed with assistive-technology users.

history.summary: New package, a one-lesson pilot of layer 2 of the wet-lab practice track: an original reading on hemocytometer counting and trypan-blue viability (sampling and dilution, Improved-Neubauer geometry, boundary and stain decisions, concentration and viability, Poisson counting uncertainty, chamber disagreement and systematic error, limits of dye exclusion) with two worked examples, 12 practice items, four retrieval cards and one self-check case, linked to the hemocytometer bench simulation. Sources: Marienfeld counting-chamber documents, Student (1907), Strober (2015) and BMBL Appendix H; scope compared with MIT OCW 20.109 Spring 2010. Lessons 1–3 and 5–8 of the outline are not written. Partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added outline lesson 1, aseptic technique: an original reading on Class II cabinet airflow, clean-to-dirty layout, pre-work checks, sterile-to-sterile manipulation, sterility incubation, mollicute detection, antibiotic limits, containment and waste; two worked examples; 12 practice items; four retrieval cards; one self-check case; and the aseptic-medium-change bench simulation. The package is now a two-lesson partial covering outline lessons 1 and 4. Sources: FDA aseptic-processing guidance (adapted), Geraghty et al. 2014 (link-only reference), current BMBL Appendix H (adapted) and MIT OCW 20.109 as a link-only comparator. Partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added outline lessons 2 and 3 in Phase A: original media-preparation and passaging readings; 24 public formative practice items (16 and 14 points respectively); eight retrieval cards; two zero-point self-check cases; the 14-checkpoint supplemented-medium filtration/QC simulation; and the 16-checkpoint adherent target-density passage simulation. Suspension passaging is conceptual only. Eagle (1955) is a metadata-only link-only bibliographic citation; its article body was neither retrieved nor read and no methods, results or historical-role claim is based on it. Geraghty et al. (2014), six Thermo Fisher pages and MIT OCW 20.109 are link-only references/comparators; FDA sterility-incubation guidance remains an attributed US-federal-work adaptation. Partial, unreviewed and formative-only; no competency or physical-validation claim.

Added outline lessons 5 and 6 jointly in Phase B: original cryopreservation/thawing and contamination/mycoplasma/authentication readings; 24 public formative items (14 and 17 points respectively); eight retrieval cards; two zero-point self-check cases; and 15- and 13-checkpoint synthetic freeze/thaw and contamination-diagnosis simulations. The package now has six lessons, 72 items and 92 practice points, 24 cards and six cases. Cryopreservation values and outcomes are synthetic; stock remains quarantined pending QC and identity reference-on-file evidence. Contamination scenarios require all five linked flasks to be inspected and quarantined before interventions; clear release requires both reviewed disposition and learner-recorded STR match. Thermo Fisher, AAAS, Springer Nature, Drexler & Uphoff, Geraghty, ANSI/ATCC and ICLAC materials are link-only; Mazur full text and Lovelock subscription full text were unavailable, the paid ATCC standard was not accessed, and no ICLAC v14 register rows or dataset were copied. MIT OCW 20.109 remains a link-only comparator. Partial, unreviewed and formative-only; no project, competency or physical-validation claim.

Joint Phase C 0.5.0 adds lessons 7 and 8 to the 0.4.0 baseline: synthetic hPSC maintenance with public scoring evidence and request-gated QC, plus records/traceability instruction. The resulting eight-lesson/eight-instructional-week package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only, with no scored project and no competency, clinical or physical-validation claim.

limitations: All eight outlined lessons are present, but this remains an eight-lesson partial package, not a reviewed or measured cell-culture course. It is unreviewed and formative-only, with no graded assessment, project, measured workload or qualified review.
Of the 33 numerical answers, 0 require units, 17 check significant figures and 0 check dimensions.

Practice items and simulations test decisions, calculations and contamination reasoning, not hand skill. Real aseptic manipulation, medium preparation, passaging, focusing, recognising cells and debris, pipetting and loading a chamber need supervised bench work.

Lesson 4's top/left boundary convention, loading steps and simulation ranges are teaching choices; the manufacturer documents read do not prescribe them. Real counting procedures, density ranges and acceptance limits come from the device instructions and each laboratory's procedures.

Lesson 1's T-75 working volume, clean-to-dirty zones, one-bottle rule, expired-label scenario, hidden-event probabilities, visible-growth threshold and simplified mycoplasma assay are teaching choices, not laboratory acceptance criteria or a validated sterility method.

Lesson 2's synthetic 500 mL formulation, QC windows, volume-weighted osmolality approximation, 98% recovery, control volume, dates, 14-day expiry, hidden events and simplified assays are simulation choices, not laboratory acceptance criteria or physical validation.
Lesson 3 teaches suspension passaging conceptually but simulates only an adherent T-75 target-density workflow; it does not model suspension vessels, shaking, growth or centrifugation choices.

Lesson 3 confluence thresholds, exact T-75 volumes, dissociation-time bound, viability penalties, target density, PDL convention and numerical tolerances are simulation choices, not laboratory acceptance criteria or physical validation.
All cells, labels, counts, media batches and contamination events are synthetic. Nothing here establishes competency, qualification or authorisation to handle human or other primate cells.
Lesson 5 uses a simplified DMSO slow-freeze/vapour-storage workflow; it does not teach vitrification, every cryoprotectant, cell-specific optimisation, full QC release or a complete cell-banking SOP.

Lesson 5 volumes, temperatures, timing bounds, hidden recovery values, DMSO-removal efficiency, viability multipliers and numerical tolerances are simulation choices, not laboratory acceptance criteria or physical validation. Dye-exclusion recounts do not establish future growth, identity, sterility or release suitability.

Lesson 6 uses synthetic organisms, visible panels, four-locus STR profiles, binary assay outputs, source assignments and dispositions; these are simulation choices, not laboratory acceptance criteria, diagnostic performance or physical validation.

The lesson’s shared-call percentage is not the Tanabe or Masters algorithm or an ASN-0002 decision threshold. Real authentication needs declared algorithms, suitable reference provenance, quality review and privacy controls; STR does not establish sterility or phenotype.

Lesson 7 is a synthetic maintenance decision loop only. It does not authorize or certify hPSC work, establish physical technique or competency, replace institutional biosafety/ethics review, or predict real growth, viability, morphology, functional pluripotency or genomic stability.

Lesson 7 density windows, three-day rhythm, differentiation areas and penalties, clump counts, handling values, five-passage QC interval, hidden events and categorical results are simulation choices, not laboratory acceptance criteria. ISSCR Standards/perspective and ATCC remain link-only; no source protocol or standards text is adapted or reproduced.
Lesson 8 teaches synthetic record joins and ledger arithmetic only; it intentionally has no bench protocol or model and therefore contributes no protocol link or checkpoint count.

Lesson 8 names ALCOA and outlines incidents/deviations, but deeper document control, audit trails, investigations, corrective and preventive action, GLP and CLIA remain deferred to planned layer-4 lab-quality-systems and institutional procedures.
The common-lot trace is an original synthetic reasoning example: a shared exposure is an investigation lead, not causal proof, physical validation or an institutional release decision.

Deeper stem-cell methods, automated counting/viability methods and full quality-system records, GLP/CLIA and investigations remain outside this package; lesson 8 hands those quality topics to planned layer-4 lab-quality-systems.
intentionally_omitted: Graded assessments, a project, measured workload and review by a qualified person.

Species identification, real diagnostic performance, a complete ASN-0002 implementation and physical rescue efficacy remain outside lesson 6; contamination response, mycoplasma evidence and bounded synthetic STR authentication are taught.
Automated cell counters, flow-cytometric and fluorescent viability assays, which are named but not taught.
Deeper quality-system documentation, investigations, corrective/preventive action, GLP and CLIA, reserved for planned layer 4 and institutional procedures.
No lesson-8 bench protocol, model, simulator link or checkpoint count; this is an intentional outline decision, not a missing integration artifact.
